- **fix(api):** DeepSeek V4's native `max` reasoning tier is now reachable. DeepSeek accepts `reasoning_effort` `low`/`high`/`max` and maps `medium`/`xhigh` down to `high`, while OmniRoute's canonical vocabulary collapses `max` onto `xhigh` — so `{"effort":"max"}` silently resolved to `high` and the catalog never advertised a `max` tier (or its `<model>-max` variant). Following the existing `extendCodexGpt56EffortValues` precedent, the native tier is now preserved for `deepseek`/`ds` V4 models only; the global effort vocabulary is unchanged, routed namespaces (`openrouter/deepseek/…`, `tllm/deepseek_v4`, `oc/deepseek-v4-flash-free`) keep the canonical behavior, and an explicit client `reasoning_effort` still wins ([#10230](https://github.com/diegosouzapw/OmniRoute/pull/10230)) — thanks @Neuron-Mr-White
- Honor provider proxies for The Old LLM Vercel blocks ([#7380](https://github.com/diegosouzapw/OmniRoute/pull/7380)) — thanks @JxnLexn

- **fix(resilience):** a bare, unrecognized `403` from a no-credential (`authType:"none"`) provider like mimocode or theoldllm no longer permanently bans the connection ([#6315](https://github.com/diegosouzapw/OmniRoute/issues/6315), [#6345](https://github.com/diegosouzapw/OmniRoute/issues/6345)) — `classifyProviderError()`'s 403 branch only exempted `apikey` providers from the terminal `FORBIDDEN` classification, so these free/stateless proxies (no real account/credential to revoke) fell through to `FORBIDDEN` on the first unmatched 403 and got `isActive:false, testStatus:"banned"` with no cooldown or retry. The exemption now also covers `authType:"none"` providers, returning `null` (recoverable) so the existing connection-cooldown/retry layer handles it. Regression guard: `tests/unit/errorClassifier-noauth-403-6315.test.ts`.

- **feat(providers):** refresh The Old LLM (Free) model catalog ([#5181](https://github.com/diegosouzapw/OmniRoute/issues/5181)) — seed the current free `/api/chatgpt` tier (GPT-5/5.1/5.2/5.3/5.4, o3/o4-mini, Gemini 3 Pro / 2.5 Pro / 2.0 Flash / 1.5 Flash, Claude 4.6 Opus/Sonnet & 4.5 Haiku, GPT-4o, Grok 4, DeepSeek V3/R1, Sonar Pro) while keeping the legacy alias IDs for saved-preference compatibility. Regression guard: `tests/unit/theoldllm-model-refresh-5181.test.ts`. (thanks @WslzGmzs)

- **fix(theoldllm):** `X-Request-Token` generated server-side, dropping the Playwright dependency — replicates the site's client `rie()` token (djb2 hash + `oldllm-client-2026` seed + UA prefix + 8-hex `crypto.randomUUID` suffix) directly, so The Old LLM no longer needs a headless browser to mint tokens. - **feat(dashboard):** quota pools can now be scheduled. Each pool takes a list of time windows (days of the week + hours, in an IANA zone of its own) saying when OmniRoute may use its accounts: an `allow` window turns the pool into a whitelist, a `block` window is a blackout that always wins over an overlapping `allow`. - **feat(providers):** add `expiry-first`, a per-provider account fallback strategy that spends the quota closest to being lost. It ranks each account by how much it must burn per hour to avoid wasting its leftover at the next reset (`usable / hoursUntilNearestReset`), so a full account whose window closes soon outranks an equally full one that holds for days, while a nearly empty account never wins on its near reset alone. `fill-first` drains the top-priority account and lets the rest roll over unspent; on a four-account Codex pool that left an 88% account untouched through a reset. Distinct from `reset-aware`, whose `resetUrgency * (1 - remaining)` term is a recovery signal and saturates to zero outside the nominal window length. Session stickiness and prompt-cache affinity are untouched; accounts within `expiryFirstTieBandPercent` rotate least-recently-used. - **feat(dashboard):** synced/imported models can now carry a manual context-window override. Rows imported through a provider's **/models** import had no edit affordance at all, so the override `#4125` added for _custom_ models was unreachable for them — even though `PUT /api/provider-models` has always accepted `contextWindowOverride` for a model with no `customModels` row, and the runtime already prefers the override. The read path was the other half of the gap: `GET /api/provider-models` attached overrides only to custom-model rows, so a value stored for a synced model could never be read back. The GET now returns the provider's overrides directly, and the passthrough row renders the same 🪟 badge and inline editor, with `#4125` semantics unchanged — a positive whole number sets the override, blank clears it and the model falls back to the discovered value. This is the correction path for third-party OpenAI-compatible aggregators whose discovery metadata understates context length (#14337). ([#14356](https://github.com/diegosouzapw/OmniRoute/pull/14356)) — thanks @abhisheksharma2411

- **fix(providers):** A Google Cloud Code / Antigravity `403 VALIDATION_REQUIRED` ("Verify your account to continue") no longer permanently bans the connection — the phrase was in `ACCOUNT_DEACTIVATED_SIGNALS`, so a single transient occurrence parked a healthy, fully-quota'd account as `banned` (`permanent: true`, 1-year cooldown, never auto-recovers). Measured on a live deployment: one Antigravity connection returned 33 of these 403s inside 10 minutes and stayed `active`, while a sibling holding 100 % of its quota on all 17 windows was banned by exactly one — the only difference being which attempt happened to be served. The phrase now lives in a new non-terminal `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED_SIGNALS` table (`open-sse/services/errorClassifier.ts`, home of the 403 branch that consumes it) and classifies as recoverable `PROJECT_ROUTE_ERROR`, which also un-blocks the cloud-code project-route recovery added for Gemini Code Assist (#868, #6452) — it was unreachable for this wording because `accountDeactivated` is evaluated first. - **fix(compression):** RTK no longer drops diagnostic lines at truncation because of three disagreeing severity vocabularies. The engine hard cap (`index.ts::defaultPriorityPatterns`), the filter priority set built from `preserve.errorPatterns` / `preserve.summaryPatterns`, and `rawOutput.ts::isLikelyFailureOutput` each carried its own word list, and the keep stage fed by `rules.includePatterns` truncated before any priority pattern was consulted — so a `2026-09-20 12:07:04 FATAL deployment aborted - rollback required` line was classified as failure output worth retaining while the compressed body dropped it, and a bare `TS2345` line was protected by the filter layer but not by the engine. They now derive from one shared vocabulary (`engines/rtk/severityVocabulary.ts`, 23 words), and diagnostic lines bypass the keep stage without populating a filter's EMPTY `includePatterns` (which would switch the stage on and newly drop every non-severity line). Measured through `processRtkText` at the live `maxCharsPerResult` on ~250-char lines: 0/55 builtin filters kept all eight severity words before, 55/55 after. Token impact is neutral — same output length, only _which_ lines survive. Reported in [#14648](https://github.com/diegosouzapw/OmniRoute/issues/14648). ([#14845](https://github.com/diegosouzapw/OmniRoute/pull/14845)) — thanks @yelsoft16

- **fix(usage):** Non-streaming responses from every Claude-format provider now store the full prompt total, not only responses served under the `claude`/`anthropic`/`vertex*`/`anthropic-compatible*` ids ([#14878](https://github.com/diegosouzapw/OmniRoute/pull/14878)). Notable affected providers: kimi-coding, deepseek, xiaomi-mimo, zai, github (Claude through `/v1/messages`), poe, agentrouter, bailian-coding-plan, and opencode-go/opencode-zen models that target the Claude format. Anthropic `usage.input_tokens` excludes prompt-cache reads and writes. Those bodies fell through to the Responses API branch of the usage extractor, which stored `input_tokens` alone next to the cache counters. The cost calculator then subtracted the cache from an input that never contained it, so fresh input tokens were billed at $0 and stored input did not match the streaming path. The extractor now recognises an Anthropic Messages body (`type: "message"`) by its shape and stores input + cache read + cache creation, as the streaming path already did. Semantic-cache replays of OpenAI answers cached for Claude clients also recover their full prompt total. Providers that report no cache counters (e.g. devin-cli-agentic) keep them as N/A instead of 0. Responses API usage (whose `input_tokens` already includes the cache), OpenAI chat and Gemini usage are unchanged. — thanks @fouadSalkini

- **fix(cursor):** the Cursor agent transport now honours the configured proxy. It talks raw HTTP/2 through `http2.connect()`, which opens its own socket and therefore bypassed both the global fetch proxy patch and the undici dispatcher — a provider proxy set in the dashboard (and `HTTPS_PROXY`) was silently ignored and Cursor traffic egressed on the host IP. A CONNECT tunnel (TLS-wrapped for `https://` proxies) or a SOCKS4/4a/5/5h tunnel is now opened first and handed to http2 via `createConnection`; proxy selection reuses `resolveProxyForRequest()`, so precedence, `NO_PROXY` and local-address bypasses match every other egress path. SOCKS setup now honours aborts, and abort/stream close releases the established tunnel. ([#14735](https://github.com/diegosouzapw/OmniRoute/pull/14735)) — thanks @MikeTuev

- **fix(cursor):** model discovery now resolves the connection's configured proxy before calling Cursor's `AvailableModels`, rather than sending the import request directly. ([#14735](https://github.com/diegosouzapw/OmniRoute/pull/14735)) — thanks @MikeTuev

- **fix(cursor):** an agent harness no longer loops on the same step. When Cursor asked to run one of its built-in tools (Read / Shell / Write), OmniRoute bridged it to the declared client tool but told Cursor the exec had been **rejected** — so the model believed its own tool never ran and retried the same step on the next turn (reported as an agent re-reading a missing file forever). Those execs are now held open and answered with a typed success carrying the client's actual output (`ReadResult.success`, `ShellResult.success`, `WriteResult.success`), the way Cursor's own CLI does. Grep, Ls, Write and Fetch built-ins also gained bridges, and the decoder now keeps their arguments (`GrepArgs.pattern/path/glob`, `WriteArgs.file_text`) instead of dropping them. ([#14737](https://github.com/diegosouzapw/OmniRoute/pull/14737)) — thanks @MikeTuev

- **fix(cursor):** complete the Cursor CLI exec replies and bridge compatible PI tools; preserve parallel tool results and return errors for unsupported requests. Forward model effort, cache usage and Responses cache-write metrics, expose selectable Grok effort variants, and allow longer bounded readiness for long agent histories. ([#14737](https://github.com/diegosouzapw/OmniRoute/pull/14737)) — thanks @MikeTuev

- **fix(cursor):** tool calling through the `cursor` provider works again. Any request whose model invoked a tool hung until `CURSOR_STREAM_TIMEOUT_MS` and returned `502 cursor-agent stream timed out`; when it did not hang, the model reported the OmniRoute tool namespace as unavailable and fell back to Cursor's built-ins, so harnesses such as opencode stalled. The agent protocol is now aligned with the `agent.v1` schema embedded in the Cursor Agent CLI: tools go on `RequestContext.tools` (field 7, not `rules` on field 2) and are advertised as an `McpDescriptor` through `mcp_meta_tool_options`, the blocking `mcp_state_exec_args` (field 36) handshake is answered, `span_context` (field 19) is no longer mistaken for the event variant, Responses-API (flat) tool definitions are read, and a Cursor built-in shell exec is bridged to the client's shell tool instead of failing closed on the timeouts Cursor stamps on every exec. ([#14737](https://github.com/diegosouzapw/OmniRoute/pull/14737)) — thanks @MikeTuev

- **Security — data directory permissions (GHSA-2pg2-xm9r-8544):** the CLI created `~/.omniroute` (or `DATA_DIR`) and wrote `.env` — which holds `STORAGE_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, the key to every stored credential — without an explicit mode, so under the common `umask 002` they landed as `0775`/`0664` and any local user could read the key and the database. First runs now create the directory `0700` and write `.env` `0600` (also when migrating Electron's `server.env`), and every run that touches encrypted storage repairs existing installs: world access is removed from the directory and `.env`/`server.env` become `0600`. Group bits on the directory are kept so deliberate group shares keep working; informational commands (`--version`, `--help`) never touch the directory. ([#14712](https://github.com/diegosouzapw/OmniRoute/pull/14712))

- **Security (GHSA-mh4f-3xj9-4gc4):** `server.env` — which holds the generated `JWT_SECRET`, `STORAGE_ENCRYPTION_KEY` and `API_KEY_SECRET` — was written by `scripts/build/bootstrap-env.mjs` (dev/start, Docker) and by the desktop app without an explicit mode, so under the usual umask it came out 0644 in a 0755 directory. Both writers now create the data dir 0700 and `server.env` 0600, and repair a file an earlier version left world-readable on every start (the file is only rewritten when a secret is missing). Follow-up to GHSA-2pg2-xm9r-8544; the package-root `.env` no longer receives generated secrets since #11436. Reported by @peterbussch. - **Security (GHSA-9p9m-h9rj-rhhg, critical):** pre-request middleware hooks ran in a `vm` context built from host objects, so hook code could reach the server realm — directly (`this.constructor.constructor("return process")()` returned the host `process`) and by polluting the server's `Object.prototype`, which a later `worker_threads` Worker inherits as `env` (`NODE_OPTIONS=--require …`). Hooks now run in an isolated realm created from a null-prototype object: the request context goes in and the result, mutated context and log lines come back only as JSON strings, and the host never awaits or calls anything from the realm. The hook contract is unchanged except that the non-JS globals `URL` / `URLSearchParams` are no longer provided inside hooks. Reported by @alienkeric. ([#14916](https://github.com/diegosouzapw/OmniRoute/pull/14916))

- **fix(budget):** a spent dollar budget no longer disables flat-rate capacity. The budget is scoped by `apiKeyId` and was enforced at the api-key policy phase, before any provider was resolved — so once the allowance was gone, a subscription/coding-plan provider that costs nothing per call was rejected alongside the metered APIs, and a mixed combo could not fall back to it. The chat path now defers the metered budget to the candidate boundary (`enforceApiKeyPolicy(..., { meteredBudget: "defer-to-candidate" })`) and re-applies it per resolved provider, before a credential is selected: a candidate that draws on the allowance is refused, one that does not stays eligible and is chosen by the normal ranking. Nothing else moves — the budget can only remove a candidate, never nominate one. Unauthorized metered spend is still prevented (an unknown provider counts as metered, and a request with no eligible non-metered candidate fails closed without dispatching), the refusal is tagged `BUDGET_EXCEEDED` so the combo loop never cools a healthy account for it, and flat-rate traffic no longer draws the allowance down while remaining fully visible in cost analytics. Every other endpoint keeps enforcing the budget at the policy phase, unchanged. ([#14348](https://github.com/diegosouzapw/OmniRoute/pull/14348)) — thanks @valimwiliam2020-art

- **fix(proxy):** the reachability fast-fail probe now uses port 80 for `http` proxies that omit one ([#14157](https://github.com/diegosouzapw/OmniRoute/issues/14157)). Proxies with explicit non-default ports are unaffected. ([#14184](https://github.com/diegosouzapw/OmniRoute/pull/14184)) — thanks @gonisulaimann

- **Security (GHSA-cqwr-7mqw-chr9):** the MITM / Agent Bridge sudo helper wrote the operator's sudo password and the command's data to the same stdin. When sudo did not prompt (a `NOPASSWD` rule, or a credential still cached from an earlier sudo), `sudo -S tee -a /etc/hosts` appended the **sudo password to the world-readable `/etc/hosts`**. The password now goes only to `sudo -S -v` (validate, runs no command), and the elevated command runs as `sudo -n <cmd>` with only its own data on stdin; hosts that never cache credentials (`timestamp_timeout=0`) fall back to a single `sudo -S` call, where sudo is certain to consume the password line.
